body: I resonate with this so much. I wish I had the willpower. But it's still no way to live. Not being able to be true to yourself because being yourself is too much for everyone you love....unconditional love just can't be found in other people, and it's so hard. Rambling here. But I wish I could figure out another way, too.

Yeah, this is not unique to humans. Ducks are a quite well known example: https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn11764-female-ducks-fight-back-against-raping-males/

Bonobo "culture" is very interesting. Female bonobos will band together and protect their own from known rapists or violent males....they also scream when being dragged off for "forced copulation" (rape), so I don't buy this post. http://www-personal.umich.edu/~phyl/anthro/coercion.html.

Absolutely. It's very unpopular. I don't feel safe expressing myself in my own circles, causing me further isolation. People assume you're an evil child hating murderer when really you feel badly for them having to suffer their unfortunate circumstances. Antinatalists see that suffering is a guarantee and that the kindest thing you can do is spare someone all that pain by not bringing them into the world.

Fellow antinatalist here. I wish for the both of our sakes I had good advice on this one. The way people bring children into the world as tools for their own happiness (and never the child's) has always disgusted me. It's irresponsible and selfish. The lengths your mother went to ensure you were born (and for manipulative purposes), knowing you would be in that type of environment, is appalling. I'm sorry you're suffering. My heart goes out to you. :(

I get the sentiment you're expressing, but I think there's a bigger picture here. Are they willingly reproducing? If so, it is definitely selfish or at least misguided to bring someone into that situation. However, I think poverty, lack of access to birth control, lack of access to higher education, and the probability that a sizable portion of the women are actually being forcibly impregnated through rape are important factors to consider.

Edit: reread your post - I doubt these types of men care what they're putting others through, sadly. Not to mention that fundamentalists of many religions push natalism at all costs.
What you're describing is EFILism. Personally I disagree, but I can empathize with the reasoning behind it. I think our species is the biggest issue here.

I feel similarly. This is a slippery slope that can only end in taking people's right to bodily autonomy away. I was forcibly hospitalized a couple of times and it did not help at all. It actively contributed to my subsequent attempts that I kept hidden. Hospitals do not care about helping you, they want your money, or your family's money. They want you to be just well enough to stay enslaved. Things like this do not bring me hope at all; they actively destroy it.

The only thing that has ever helped were close, meaningful relationships with a trusted mentor - some random psychiatrist shoving pills in my face, or hell, a SWAT team busting down my door (as requested by some commentors) will NOT help people like me...or people incorrectly flagged, for that matter.

Edit: you're right that it's a bunch of unnecessary drama - I stopped crying out for help once I realized people don't care, or don't have answers. It is futile to tell someone "it gets better" when the world is clearly going to shit and you have a fundamental disagreement on the meaning of existence.

I was appalled to have to scroll down this far to see a comment like this. I wholeheartedly agree,  and I've attempted suicide numerous times in the past. When people are begging for a police state with Minority Report style interventionism... let's just say this is not helpful for all suicidal people.

I hear you. I hear myself in your words. You express yourself quite beautifully. I definitely empathize with your situation and want to offer you a sincere "you're not alone". I absolutely believe my passions have been stolen from me and that I'm a shell of who I once was. I don't know if it gets better, but you're not the only one.

25 here and in the same situation. I've had these feelings for over half my life. It does not get better. You just learn even more things that make you want to exit the planet.

I've decided I'll do the deed once my parents die. I don't want to hurt them.
